newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, FRANCE HOLD TALKS ON THOMSON SALE.
newsitem.headline: EU, FRANCE HOLD TALKS ON THOMSON SALE.

text.p: The European Commission and France are holding discussions over the privatisation of defence and electronics giant Thomson SA .
European Union officials said a "technical meeting" had already taken place, after the French authorities informed the EU of the planned sale of Thomson to the Lagardere group.

The deal must be assessed by the EU because the French state intends to inject 11 billion francs in the loss-making company before selling it for a symbolic franc. This has apparently raised the attention of Philips , a competitor of Thomson's consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
Largardere plans to sell Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
"They (Philips) have called the Commission," an EU source said, adding that the Dutch group was sounding out the Commission rather than complaining about the plan.
French daily newspaper Les Echos said on Tuesday that Philips had complained to the Commission about the Thomson plan.
But a Philips spokesman also told Reuters in Amsterdam: "We have no plans to launch a complaint on this. This is the sort of thing the Commission looks into in its own way."
As the EU's competition watchdog, the Commission must ensure that the capital injection will not give Thomson an unfair advantage vis-a-vis its rivals.

The French government said in October it agreed to Lagardere's takeover proposal for Thomson and has announced since that the company, which is expected to have 28 billion francs of debt at the end of 1996, would be recapitalised with 11 billion francs.
A final decision must be taken by the French parliament's privatisation commission in December.
Its responsibility is to ensure that the government's financial interest is respected in any privatisation.
There was no indication as to when the Commission will make its own judgement on the capital injection.
As to the sale itself, it will have a month from the moment the deal is formally notified to decide whether to give its green light or start an in-depth four-month probe.
